en: The Vow of the Great Zen Master Daiman Huisi of Mount Nanyue.

I have heard it thus: In the *Sūtra on the Original Arising of the Śākyamuni Buddha’s Samādhi of the Gate of Compassion and His Contemplation of Sentient Beings*, it is said that the Buddha entered the womb on the seventh day of the seventh month of the year of Gui-chou. Until...
He was born on the eighth day of the fourth month in the year of Jiǎyīn.
By the year of Rénshēn, he was nineteen years old;
on the eighth day of the second month, he left the household life (renounced the world).
In the year Kǐwèi, at the age of thirty,
he attained the Way on the eighth day of the twelfth month of that winter.
He reached the age of eighty in the year Kǐyǒu.
On the fifteenth day of the second month, he entered *parinirvāṇa* through skillful means.
The True Dharma shall remain for a full five hundred years, from the year Jiǎxū to the year Guīsì.
The Semblance Dharma shall endure for a full one thousand years, from the year Jiawu to Guiyou.
The Final Dharma shall endure for a full ten thousand years, from the year Jiashu to Guichou.
After nine thousand eight hundred years have passed into the age of the Final Dharma (mappō),
the Bodhisattva Candraprabha shall appear in the land of China (Zhendan) to preach the Dharma and deliver sentient beings on a vast scale.
Fifty-two years after his entry into nirvana, [the prophecy shall be fulfilled].
In the Śūraṅgama Sūtra and the Pratyutpanna Samādhi Sūtra, [the teachings] first cease and disappear;
in other sūtras, they cease in succession; and in the Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra, they remain for a hundred years after which they cease and depart until the age of great evil arrives.
I now vow to uphold this so that it shall not perish,
teaching and transforming sentient beings until the appearance of Maitreya Buddha.
This was after the Buddha entered nirvana in the year of Guiyou.
When Maitreya attains Buddhahood at the beginning of the future Bhadrakalpa, there will be fifty-six billion years remaining;
from the very start of the Dharma-ending age, I have established this great vow.
He practiced asceticism in this manner for five hundred and sixty million years,
making a firm vow that he would fulfill the merits of the Buddha-way and behold Maitreya Buddha.
As stated in his *Wish-Fulfilling Vow*, there was nothing he did not practice in order to enter the Path.
He cultivated the practice of dhyāna early on and studied the propagation of the sutras for a short time.
During this interval, however, obstacles and adverse circumstances were manifold.
A Brief Record of the Original Source, Together with the Formulation of Vows and the Creation of Two Sets of Scriptures in Golden Characters.
I bow my head and take refuge in all Buddhas of the ten directions.
I bow my head and take refuge in the twelve divisions of the scriptures.
I bow my head and take refuge in all the great Bodhisattvas and the assembly of worthy and holy ones of the forty-two stages.
I bow my head and take refuge in all the Pratyekabuddhas.
To the assembly of Śrāvakas, both those in training and those beyond training;
and furthermore, I prostrate to Brahmā, Śakra, the Four Heavenly Kings, and the eight classes of devas, nāgas, and others.
The Great General of the Dharma-protecting Good Deities of the Dark Void,
Huisi reflected to himself:
"Since beginningless time, I have possessed this consciousness."
Because they do not plant the roots of untainted goodness,
they are constantly led astray by craving and views;
shrouded by ignorance, they are caused to fall into falsehood.
Birth and death increase daily as the wheel of suffering constantly turns without ever resting.
Wandering through the five destinies, one causes the six consciousnesses to revolve through the six realms.
Thus far, one has not encountered the appearance of Śākyamuni in this world.
Furthermore, I have not yet been graced by Maitreya’s three assemblies;
I dwell amidst the difficulties of being among those who come before and after.
Yet, I rely upon the power of my slight roots of goodness from the past.
In the final age of Śākyamuni, having obtained a human body,
one reverently upholds what has been proclaimed in the holy teachings.
Śākyamuni Buddha preached the Dharma and remained in the world for over eighty years.
Having guided and benefited sentient beings until his conditions for transformation were exhausted, he entered parinirvāṇa.
After his parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma remained in the world for five hundred years;
once the True Dharma had vanished, the Semblance Dharma remained in the world for one thousand years.
After the Semblance Dharma has ceased, the Final Dharma will remain in the world for ten thousand years.
I, Huisi, am currently in the eighty-second year of this Final Dharma period;
the year is Yimwei, on the eleventh day of the eleventh month.
He was born in Wujin County, Ruyang Commandery, Nanyuzhou, within the Great Wei Kingdom.
Upon reaching the age of fifteen, he left the household life to practice the Way,
reciting the Lotus Sūtra and various Mahāyāna scriptures.
Practicing asceticism with diligence until he reached the age of twenty,
he observed that the world is impermanent and that many sentient beings die;
thereupon, he reflected within himself.
This body is impermanent, suffering, empty, and devoid of self or person; it lacks autonomy.
Subject to arising and ceasing, decaying and disintegrating, its manifold sufferings never cease.
It is truly most terrifying.
Worldly phenomena are like clouds; conditioned things are difficult to trust.
Those who cling to them are burned by the great fire of afflictions, whereas those who relinquish them attain the great bliss of unconditioned nirvana.
All sentient beings have lost their way on the right path and possess no mind of renunciation;
for the sake of these beings and for my own sake, I have resolved to attain liberation,
giving rise to the bodhicitta and establishing great vows.
If one seeks all the supernatural powers (abhijñā) of the Tathāgata,
how can one deliver others without first realizing them oneself?
One must first train and attain realization before being able to practice [for the sake of others].
Seeking the fruit of the Way for oneself in order to deliver immeasurable sentient beings throughout the ten directions;
for the sake of severing all the afflictions of all sentient beings throughout the ten directions;
and in order to cause immeasurable sentient beings throughout the ten directions [to attain liberation].
Because they have thoroughly penetrated all dharma-gates,
and because they desire to bring to fulfillment the path to bodhi for all immeasurable sentient beings throughout the ten directions,
they seek the unsurpassed path as the foremost *śūraṅgama*.
He traveled throughout the various great Chan masters of the Qi state to study the Mahāyāna.
He constantly dwelt in forests and wilds, practicing walking meditation and dhyāna.
At the age of thirty-four, he was engaged in doctrinal debate within the borders of Yanzhou in Henan.
Consequently, he encountered several wicked bhikṣus who administered a potent, poisonous drug to Huìsī to consume;
his entire body became putrid and his five viscera were likewise rotted away.
On the verge of death, he was restored to life once more.
My original intention was to cross the river and visit all the Chan masters; midway,
I encountered this malicious poison that has incapacitated me.
Disgusted with these verbal explanations and realizing they obstructed the Path,
he immediately took his remaining provisions and returned to Xinzhou, no longer crossing the river.
With single-minded devotion, he entered deep into the mountains.
While he was about to depart, the Regional Inspector of Xinzhou,
together with various prefects and magistrates, earnestly entreated him to remain,
establishing a Zen retreat and expounding the meaning of the Mahāyāna.
Three years have passed without a moment’s rest.
Xu Chang in Liangzhou has again sent an invitation,
and furthermore, the Prefect of Xinzhou wishes to send a memorial.
As they were about to return to Ye County, Huìsī’s resolve was firm; he did not wish to travel north.
Desiring instead to journey south, he immediately left the assembly and crossed over to stay in the mountains south of the Huái River.
From the age of twenty until thirty-eight,
he constantly resided south of the Yellow River to study the Mahāyāna,
personally attending upon and making offerings to various great Chan masters.
He traveled through various provinces and did not reside in a single place.
At that time, by imperial decree, all the Chan masters within the realm were summoned to the palace for offerings.
Huisi reflected upon himself.
Foolish and lacking in virtue,
he was unwilling to follow the imperial decree to find a means of relinquishing his position and taking refuge;
instead, he crossed the Huai River and entered the mountains, remaining there until he reached the age of thirty-nine.
In the one hundred and twentieth year of the Dharma-ending age,
Liu Huibao, the Regional Inspector of Yingzhou in Huainan, traveled together with him in the mountains of Yingzhou and invited him out to lecture on the meaning of the Mahāyāna.
At that time, because he answered according to the meaning of the principles,
several Dharma masters became greatly incensed.
Five heterodox teachers placed a medicinal preparation of raw gold within their food and drink, intending for Huisi to eat it.
The remaining scraps were eaten by three people, who died on the very same day.
At that time, Huìsī’s body was in extreme distress;
he was able to remain for seven days before his life-breath was about to expire.
At the moment of death, with single-minded devotion, he joins his palms toward the Buddhas of the ten directions and repents.
Recollecting the *prajñāpāramitā*, he speaks these words:
"One who lacks the knowledge of others' minds should not preach the Dharma."
When he brought this to mind, the poison of the gold was immediately eliminated and he recovered.
From that time forward, he encountered such [incidents] more than once.
When he reached the age of forty, it was the one hundred twenty-first year of the Final Dharma (mofa).
He resided at Kaeyak-sa Temple in Gwangju.
Ba-zi established five hundred households to jointly serve as the Gwangju Regional Inspector (Cishi).
"Please recite the Mahāyāna Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra once.
This was in his forty-first year, the one hundred twenty-second year of the Dharma-ending age (mofa),
while he was at Mount Dasu within the borders of Gwangju.
He lectured on the meaning of the Mahāyāna once.
When he reached the age of forty-two— this being the one hundred and twenty-third year of the Dharma-ending Age—
he was staying at Gwanip-sa Temple west of the city of Gwangju.
Furthermore, when he expounded the meaning of the Mahāyāna once,
many wicked masters of debate vied with one another to come and disturb him, giving rise to hearts of jealousy.
They all desired to kill and destroy the meaning of the Prajñāpāramitā.
At that time, I gave rise to a heart of great compassion for those evil teachers and made this vow, speaking these words:
I vow to cast the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā* and other Mahāyāna sūtras in golden letters and enshrine these scriptural volumes within caskets of lapis lazuli; furthermore,
I shall manifest infinite bodies throughout the lands of the ten directions to preach this sūtra.
He caused all the evil masters of heterodox doctrines to attain faith and abide in non-retrogression.
This occurred when he was forty-three years of age, during the one hundred twenty-fourth year of the Dharma-ending Age.
He was in Nanding Prefecture.
The Provincial Governor requested that he lecture on the meaning of the Mahāyāna once.
At that time, there were many heterodox masters who opposed him.
They vied with one another in giving rise to evil intentions and causing great turmoil;
furthermore, they employed various wicked means to sever the connection with donors so that they would no longer send food.
After fifty days had passed, he sent only his disciples to convert others so that he might sustain his own life.
At that time, he made this vow:
"For the sake of these people and for all sentient beings..."
He vowed to produce one volume of the Mahāyāna Prajñāpāramitā written in golden letters,
to enshrine the scroll within a casket made of pure lapis lazuli and the seven treasures,
and to provide a high throne of various jewels, a canopy of the seven treasures, and a jeweled lattice curtain.
Having made offerings of flowers, incense, necklaces, and various kinds of ritual implements to the Prajñāpāramitā,
I shall thereafter manifest immeasurable physical bodies throughout the ten directions and the six realms of existence.
Without calculating the number of kalpas until the attainment of Bodhi,
one shall preach the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra for the sake of all sentient beings in the ten directions.
In the interim, if one acts as a Dharma master like Dharmodgata,
or acts as a disciple seeking the Dharma like Sadāprarudita,
then after making this vow, all evil bhikṣus will completely withdraw and disperse.
Having made this vow, he immediately gave instructions, saying these words:
"I shall produce the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra written in golden characters.
This will be in the year forty-four, during the one hundred and twenty-fifth year of the Final Dharma."
In the year of Wuyi (the fifth year of the Great Year cycle), he returned to Mount Dasu within the borders of Gwangju and proclaimed to all quarters:
"I wish to commission the transcription of the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra in golden letters."
"It is necessary to compose a preface for this sutra;
who is capable of composing it? At that time, a bhikṣu named Saṃgharakṣita suddenly arrived of his own accord and spoke these words:
I am able to cast the *Prajñāpāramitā* Sūtra in golden letters.
Once I have obtained the beginning of the scripture, I shall travel throughout all the provinces to teach and transform them.
The provincial governors and the people within their territories—whether lay or ordained, monastic or secular—shall obtain various treasures and wealth.
He purchased gold to produce the scripture,
from the fifteenth day of the first month until the eleventh day of the eleventh month.
This was done at Jiangu Temple in Guangcheng County, within the capital city of Guangzhou, in the southern region.
Only then shall I be able to fulfill my prior vow by commissioning a copy of the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra* in golden letters,
along with a lapis lazuli jewel casket to enshrine it.
At that very moment, he made this great vow:
"By virtue of this great vow, may this *Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra* written in golden letters and its casket of seven precious gems [endure]."
No demons, nor any evil calamities, shall be able to obstruct or destroy them.
We pray that in the future, when the World-Honored One Maitreya appears in the world,
he may universally act for the sake of all immeasurable sentient beings.
When this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra is being spoken,
by the power of my vow and the golden letters, may Maitreya’s adorned world tremble in six ways, causing the great assembly to give rise to doubt.
Bowing my head, I ask the Buddha: by what causes and conditions does the great earth tremble?
I only pray that the World-Honored One will expound upon it.
At that time, Maitreya Buddha addressed his disciples: "You all should with one mind join your palms."
Listen attentively and believe with certainty: In the past there was a Buddha named Śākyamuni who appeared in the world and preached this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra to extensively deliver sentient beings.
After that World-Honored One entered parinirvāṇa...
The True Dharma and the Semblance Dharma have both already passed away; within the Final Dharma that remains in the world,
at that time the age shall be evil, the five turbidities will compete to arise,
and human life will be shortened so that it does not reach even a hundred years, as people practice the ten unwholesome deeds.
While they were thus slaying one another, at that time the *Prajñāpāramitā-sūtra* appeared in the world.
Then there was a bhikṣu named Huisi who composed this *Mahāpāramitā-sūtra*, with its characters written in gold.
Within this lapis lazuli jewel casket, I enshrine this sutra and make this great vow:
"I shall deliver and liberate immeasurable sentient beings. In the future, during the Worthy Kalpa when Maitreya appears in the world, I shall preach this Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra."
From the *Pāramitā Sūtra*: By the power of my vow and the majestic spiritual authority of this precious casket of the Golden Sūtra,
may the world of seven jewels shake in six ways, causing the great assembly to give rise to doubt, so that they may prostrate and question the Buddha.
"I only pray that you will explain the cause and conditions for this earthquake.
At that time, the Buddha, the World-Honored One, addressed the great assembly: "You should know that it is due to the power of the vows of that bhikṣu;
the golden sutra within the precious casket now desires to appear."

The great assembly addressed the Buddha: “We only pray that the World-Honored One, by means of his supernormal powers, will cause us to behold the precious casket of the golden sūtra. The Buddha said:
“You all should with one mind pay homage to the past Buddha Śākyamuni.”
One should likewise with a single mind Single-mindedly recollect the *Prajñāpāramitā-sūtra*.
When the Buddha spoke these words, The great earth again shook in six ways,
And a great radiance issued forth, Universally illuminating immeasurable worlds throughout the ten directions.
Its fragrance is exquisite and wondrous, surpassing that of sandalwood by hundreds of thousands of millions of times;
all sentient beings who smell it conceive the aspiration for enlightenment (*bodhicitta*).
A casket of lapis lazuli appears before the great assembly; it can only be seen with the eyes, and no one is able to open it.
At that time, the great assembly leaped for joy and, with one voice, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Indeed, World-Honored One, how may we behold the text of the Prajñā Sūtra?
Maitreya Buddha said: "The author of that sūtra has made a great vow."
"You all should single-mindedly contemplate him and recite his name;
you shall naturally behold him. When these words were spoken, the entire great assembly recited my name:
"Namo Huìsī! At that time, from the four directions...
Emerging from the earth, they filled the void of space;
their bodies were all golden in color, endowed with the thirty-two marks and immeasurable radiance.
All of them were those who had previously composed this sutra; by the power of the Buddha, the precious caskets opened of their own accord.
A great sound issues forth, shaking the ten directions and all worlds.
At that time, the Golden Sūtra emits a great radiance;
its immeasurable colors are like massive clouds, flowing and filling the ten directions and all worlds.
Various sounds universally proclaim to all sentient beings; furthermore, there is a wondrous fragrance that delights the hearts of the multitude.
At that time, sentient beings—by the power of my vows, by witnessing the earthquake, by seeing the radiance, and by hearing the proclamation of the fragrance and the sounds—[are awakened].
Attaining what had never been attained before, their bodies and minds were filled with joy and bliss,
like that of a bhikṣu entering the third dhyāna. At that very moment,
they all fully attained the noble path of the three vehicles, and even fully attained the knowledge of all modes (sarvākārajñatā).
If this vow is not fulfilled, I shall not attain wondrous enlightenment.

Furthermore, I vow that wherever the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones of the ten directions, preach this Prajñāpāramitā, all such places shall be exactly like the great assembly of Maitreya. Should it be so in the ten directions...
May the teachings of immeasurable Buddhas be expounded simultaneously;
may this sutra likewise be attained all at once and appear universally before me.
May each and every auspicious sign and great assembly of Buddhas equally deliver sentient beings, and may each World-Honored One do so likewise.
All shall proclaim the name of Śākyamuni as well as my own name;
just as at the great assembly of Maitreya, they shall be immeasurable. If it were not so, I would not attain wondrous enlightenment.
Furthermore, I vow that in the lands of the ten directions in the future, the caskets and the scriptural scrolls [shall be spread].
There are immeasurable names, corresponding to the various lands:
where human bodies are large, the caskets and the sutra scrolls are also large, and the characters are likewise large;
where human bodies are small, the caskets and the sutra scrolls are also small, and the characters are likewise small.
According to the lands, the essence among all treasures—those things most prized by people—is due to the power of *prajñā*.
Thus, the caskets and the sutra scrolls transform their characters into exquisite, wondrous jewels;
they never remain as mere lapis lazuli or golden letters.
The paper upon which this scripture is written is the essence of the Vajra;
it cannot be damaged until the inconceivable and immeasurable kalpas of the future,
when Buddhas appear in the worlds of the ten directions and preach this Prajñāpāramitā.
The stages of the pāramitās are likewise thus; were it otherwise, one would not attain wondrous enlightenment.
May I, in future ages, throughout the lands of the ten directions and all Buddha-worlds, be universally known by the name Śākyamuni Tathāgata.
The precious casket of the Golden Sūtra and my own name—therefore, these sounds reach throughout the ten directions and all worlds;
all sentient beings hear them universally and thereby enter the Path. Should there be any sentient beings who do not enter the Path, [it shall be because they have not heard this].
Through various skillful means and transformations of the supernormal powers, I shall subdue them and ensure they attain the Way.
If it were otherwise, I would not take up wondrous enlightenment.
Furthermore, I make this vow: "I now enter the mountains to repent for all [sins]."
Regarding the grave offenses that obstruct the Path: while practicing walking meditation and cultivating dhyāna,
if one attains the five supernatural powers (*pañcābhijñā*) of a rishi, or the six supernatural powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*),
and recites from memory the twelve divisions of the Tathāgata’s sūtras, as well as the Tripiṭaka and all non-Buddhist texts;
Thoroughly understanding the meaning of the Buddha-dharma, I manifest immeasurable bodies;
flying through the void beyond the Realm of Ultimate Form, I reach the Sphere of Neither Perception nor Non-Perception.
There, I listen to and gather the Dharma-gates preached by the various devas, and I likewise preach them to those devas.
The Buddhist sutras he held were returned to Jambudvīpa, where he expounded them extensively for the sake of humanity;
subsequently, they reached even the three miserable realms and down to the adamantine base,
such that the Dharma he upheld pervaded the trichiliocosm and the lands of the ten directions.
It is likewise thus: making offerings to all Buddhas and manifesting sovereign transformations to convert sentient beings, all these are performed simultaneously.
Were it otherwise, one would have to use exquisite sandalwood for the high throne and adorn it with various colors and patterns.
With a canopy and awning made of the seven supreme jewels, adorned with various gems that radiate light;
with the words of the sutra written in Jambūnada gold and the sutra case made of lapis lazuli and crystal;
revering the Buddha-dharma and delighting in making offerings, one then preaches the Dharma to transform sentient beings.
Without before, without after, and without middle, I practice all at once within a single thought-moment.
I now enter the mountains to study this; it is not for the sake of deluding or deceiving sentient beings.
If there are evil people who obstruct me, may they encounter inauspiciousness in their present lives.

Subjected to all manner of evil retributions, If one does not reform the mind, one will harm oneself and die to fall into hell, entering the boiling cauldrons. The karmic retribution for slandering the Dharma lasts for many kalpas;
I vow to cause them to give rise to the Bodhicitta, To uphold the precepts and cultivate goodness until they reach the site of enlightenment.
I practice this vow for the sake of sentient beings, so that the treasury of the Buddha-dharma may endure for a long time.
May wicked people who, out of envy, cause perverse disturbances and confusion, not be able to obstruct or ruin my practice.
If I am protected by virtuous people, may the various devas and benevolent spirits provide their assistance.
May they cause the protection of the Dharma to endure for a long time; may those born later in the Pure Land attain the Way of the Buddha;
may they cause the cultivation of the Path to be swiftly accomplished. With no dual mind, I have made this vow;
furthermore, I make another vow: may all the Buddhas of the ten directions bear witness to it themselves.

Now, for the sake of these two golden-lettered Mahāyāna sūtras— the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā* and the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*— and because I desire to extensively preach the Dharma throughout the ten directions,
my three karmas lack power and I have attained no mastery.
Unable to appear simultaneously throughout the ten directions to discipline body and mind and transform sentient beings,
I now enter the mountains to repent, practice dhyāna, and study as a seer of the five supernatural powers,
seeking the Unsurpassed Way so that I may first achieve its fulfillment.
Having first mastered the five supernatural powers as a rishi, one then studies the sixth supernatural power:
upholding the twelve divisions of the *sūtras* of Śākyamuni,
as well as all the Dharma treasuries of the Buddhas of the ten directions, together with all the treatise treasuries (*śāstrapiṭaka*) of the bodhisattvas.
With unimpeded eloquence, you appear universally throughout the ten directions;

Amidst this evil age, you make offerings to all Buddhas. Upholding the Dharma of Śākyamuni so that it shall not be severed, Wherever the Dharma of the Buddhas of the ten directions is about to perish, May you be present in all those places.

He maintains [the teachings] so they shall not perish, vowing to remain in this land until he is fully endowed with the ten stages and the perfection of omniscience, achieving the stage of Buddhahood. For this reason,
he first becomes a long-lived rishi and, relying on the five supernormal powers, studies the bodhisattva path.
Unless one is a divine immortal, one cannot dwell for long; For the sake of the Dharma, I study to become an immortal and do not crave longevity.
I vow that with this very body, I shall see Maitreya Buddha during the future Bhadrakalpa.
If it be otherwise, I shall not attain wondrous enlightenment.
With a sincere heart, I make this vow: May I, in the future, at the beginning of the Bhadrakalpa,
when the World-Honored One Maitreya has attained the Way of the Buddha and is preaching the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra for the great assembly,
by virtue of the power of the vow I have made this day, [attain that same state].
With an ugly form and a lowly, inferior physical body, one beholds Maitreya Buddha;
through the power of his vow, he establishes another body whose appearance and features are peerless,
surpassing those of humans and devas, endowed with immeasurable eloquence and supernormal transformations.
With sovereign mastery according to one's will, one beholds Maitreya Buddha;

with these two bodies, one sees the Buddha simultaneously. By the power of their vow, even a lowly, humble, and unattractive body can undergo transformation, fully accomplishing unimpeded supernormal powers (*abhijñā*).
The various pāramitās, inscribed in golden letters, through the power of their vows,
stand before Maitreya; the two bodies appear simultaneously,
manifesting transformations that pervade the ten directions, extensively expounding the profound Dharma of the Mahāprajñāpāramitā.
Having delivered sentient beings through the six pāramitās, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, and the supernormal powers, he suddenly vanished. He made this vow:
"May Maitreya Buddha, for the sake of the great assembly, explain the causes and conditions of my present body and the origins of my vows."
If it were not so, may I never attain Buddhahood. Furthermore, I make this vow:
I now bow my head and repent with a sincere heart for the many enmities I have created and the causes and conditions that have troubled others, from beginningless kalpas until this present life.
Seeing others practicing virtue, they create obstacles for them; they destroy the wholesome deeds of others without realizing it themselves.
Relying on their own lineage, they are heedless in the prime of their youth and oppress others with their power.
They do not contemplate the principles of reason, but instead believe in false and perverted views.
Having served non-Buddhist teachers and created many obstacles within the Triple Gem, I have long accumulated karmic offenses;
the retribution for these now manifests in this present life.
Therefore, I prostrate with a sincere heart and repent before the Buddhas of the ten directions and all the worthy sages.
Brahmā, Śakra, and the Four Heavenly Kings; the eight classes of devas, nāgas, and others;
the benevolent deities who protect the Dharma—whether dwelling in the dark or the light, in the hidden or the manifest—I pray that you act as witnesses.
May the sins that obstruct the Path be eliminated, and may body and mind be purified. From this day forth, may all that we do be auspicious.
Free from all obstacles, may I dwell in the deep mountains, contemplating the Buddha-way and aspiring to attain its profound depths.

May I obtain the various dhyānas and liberations, and through the power of supernatural faculties, repay the kindness of the Buddhas. I vow that in this very body, I shall attain non-retrogressive wisdom.
If it were not so, I vow not to attain Buddhahood. Furthermore,
I pray that in all the lands of the ten directions,
should there be the fourfold assembly— monks, nuns, and other wise ones— [may they all...]
They shall uphold, recite, and read the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra;
whether in mountain forests, wildernesses, secluded places, cities, or villages,
they shall expound and explain it for the great assembly.
There are hosts of māras who compete to come and disturb, vex, and destroy the Prajñāpāramitā.
If such a person can single-mindedly join their palms and invoke my name,
they will immediately attain immeasurable supernormal powers (abhijñā).
At that time, I also manifested as a transformed person within that assembly,
appearing as a member of his retinue and claiming to be his disciple;
I subdued the various māras and defeated all the non-Buddhists.
I shall cause that wise one to attain great renown;
at that time, I will further manifest as the fourfold assembly and appear everywhere— in mountain forests and villages— to provide protection.
Sometimes he manifests as the image of a powerful king of the ghost spirits;
sometimes as a śramaṇa;
and sometimes as a lay devotee.
Or they may become kings, ministers, or high officials,
issuing decrees throughout the land to punish all those who violate the precepts;
if there are those who are stubborn and do not reform their hearts, [they shall be dealt with accordingly].
Or they may cause them to manifest entry into the Avīci Hell;
through various forms of intense pressure, they will certainly cause them to change their minds and lead them back to take refuge in that teacher of the Dharma.
"I prostrate myself and beg you with compassion; only if you accept me as your disciple may I be released.
Let all these evil deeds be transformed into auspiciousness."
If it were not so, I would not attain wondrous enlightenment.
From the moment I first resolved my mind [for awakening], all meritorious deeds I have performed I have bestowed entirely upon sentient beings.
This shall continue until the time when the World-Honored One Maitreya appears in the world in the future.
Having fulfilled the ten stages, he enters the stainless state;
among those who receive the prediction of enlightenment, he is the foremost.
In a future age, after passing through incalculable eons, he shall attain the path of Buddhahood.
An inconceivable trichiliocosm constitutes a single buddha-field,
surpassing all the sublime and pure worlds of the ten directions and exceeding all the defiled lands beyond them.
By the power of my vows, I shall cause all sentient beings, though dwelling in a single place, to perceive their surroundings differently.
I shall subdue those who are wicked and inspire them to resolve upon Bodhicitta;
once they have so resolved, they shall see that all impurities and evils are entirely purified.
The flowers and fruits of the seven treasures are fully present according to the season,
without the distinctions of the four seasons.
The inhabitants of that land, both gods and humans, are all of one golden hue.
He possessed the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics,
and was endowed with the six supernormal powers such that he was no different from a Buddha;
yet, apart from the wisdom of a Buddha, there was none who could know him.
If it were not so, I would not attain wondrous enlightenment. Suppose I am a Buddha:
may all sentient beings of the ten directions who have made vows to be born in my land [be reborn there].
They are fully endowed with the path of Samantabhadra;
according to their original vows, they possess mastery over the length of their lives,
as well as the physical marks and signs, wisdom, and supernormal powers of their form bodies.
In teaching and transforming sentient beings, they are equal and without distinction.
Food, drink, clothing, and other necessities manifest spontaneously according to thought without the need for fabrication;
were it otherwise, one would not attain wondrous enlightenment.
If, when I attain Buddhahood,
sentient beings of the ten directions who hear my name,
uphold the precepts, and practice with diligence the six perfections, [should not all be born in my land...]
Those who uphold my vows and invoke my name,
and who wish to see my body by practicing for seven days or twenty-one days,
shall immediately behold me and have all their virtuous aspirations fulfilled.
If it were not so, I would not attain wondrous enlightenment. Suppose I am a Buddha:
if there are sentient beings in the worlds of the ten directions, and...
One who has committed the five heinous crimes and should fall into hell,
upon encountering a virtuous friend at the moment of death who instructs them to recite my name,
the sinner hears it.
With palms joined, they recite the name with an unceasing voice for the duration of ten recitations.
At the moment when life is about to end—
They shall immediately behold me;
their spirits will be welcomed to be reborn in my land, where I will preach the Mahāyāna for them.
Upon hearing this Dharma, these people will attain the patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharmakṣānti*) and shall never again fall back.
If it were not so, I would not attain wondrous enlightenment.
Should I attain Buddhahood,
my world shall be pure, free from the three evil realms, and likewise devoid of women.
All sentient beings are born by transformation.
Possessing the thirty-two marks, they fly through the air with sovereign ease.
Their radiance shines everywhere, such that there are no sun or moon.
The land of the seven treasures is free from all defilement and evil;
were it otherwise, I would not attain wondrous enlightenment.
If there are sentient beings in the great hells, [I shall save them].
Upon hearing my name, they shall immediately attain liberation;
if it were not so, I would not realize wondrous enlightenment.
If there are sentient beings who have fallen among the hungry ghosts, [they shall likewise be liberated].
For hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas, they do not even hear the names of food or drink;
they are constantly scorched by the blazing fires of hunger and undergo great suffering and distress.
Upon hearing my name, they shall immediately attain full satisfaction;
gaining the power of right mindfulness, they shall cast off their bodies as hungry ghosts and be reborn among humans and devas.
They shall resolve upon bodhicitta and reach the stage of non-retrogression.
If it were not so, one would not attain wondrous enlightenment.
If there are sentient beings who, due to evil karma,
fall among the animals and undergo various sufferings.
Upon hearing my name, all their sufferings shall be eternally extinguished;
they shall immediately obtain the upright bodies of humans and devas,
and shall immediately hear the True Dharma and become fully endowed with the Noble Path.
If it were not so, I would not attain wondrous enlightenment.
If there are sentient beings imprisoned and confined in dungeons, subjected to flogging and cruel torment,
who invoke my name and resolve their minds upon Bodhi;
Thus, one attains liberation, and even the scars of wounds are extinguished.
By means of this, one gives rise to the resolve to dwell in non-retrogression;
were it otherwise, one would not attain wondrous enlightenment.
If there are sentient beings who are unjustly bound and encounter great calamities—
whether they be guilty or innocent—
and when they are about to be executed, they call upon my name.
The swords, staves, shackles, fetters, and locks they were grasping were all completely shattered, and they immediately attained liberation;
they gave rise to the bodhicitta and dwelt in the stage of non-retrogression.
If it were not so, one would not attain wondrous enlightenment.
Throughout the ten directions, there are immeasurable sentient beings who suffer from hundreds of thousands of ailments and karmic obstructions, and whose various sense faculties are incomplete.
If one recites my name, upholds it without forgetting,
and contemplates with right mindfulness, the suffering of illness will be extinguished,
the faculties will become complete, and one will immediately recover.
If it were not so, one would not attain sublime enlightenment.
If there is a bhikṣu dwelling in mountain forests who recites the Prajñāpāramitā and other Mahāyāna sūtras, [he shall be protected].
One should practice meditative concentration and supernormal powers;
however, because of the obstructions of past karma, one may not achieve them through such practice.
Therefore, one should perform this practice three times each during the day and three times each during the night.
If one invokes the Buddhas of the ten directions and holds my name,
whatever aspirations and various requests this person makes shall be fully accomplished;
if it were otherwise, I would not attain wondrous enlightenment.
If, when I attain Buddhahood,
sentient beings of the six realms throughout the worlds of the ten directions hear my name,
they shall immediately resolve their minds upon unexcelled bodhi and abide in non-retrogression.
If it were not so, one would not attain wondrous enlightenment.
When Buddhahood is attained,
immeasurable radiance constantly illumines all things.
If any of the fourfold assembly who seek the Buddha-way hear my name and practice my vow,
they shall immediately attain the ten stages in their entirety and enter the wisdom of the Tathāgata at that very moment.
If it were not so, I would not attain wondrous enlightenment.
If I should attain Buddhahood, may all Buddhas throughout the worlds of the ten directions together praise me and proclaim my original vows as well as my Buddha-merits.
Sentient beings who hear this shall immediately receive the prediction of enlightenment.
If this vow is not fulfilled, I shall not attain wondrous awakening.
When I attain Buddhahood in a future age, [may all beings likewise receive the prediction].
As he preached the Prajñāpāramitā for the great assembly,
the worlds of the ten directions shook in six ways,
and a precious casket containing the Golden Sūtra emerged before him.
He shall expound for the great assembly the causes and conditions of his original vows;
it shall be equal to the assemblies of all Buddhas without any difference.
Were it not so, he would not attain wondrous enlightenment.
In accordance with all the vows I have previously made for the sake of seeking the Buddha-way,
I shall not calculate the number of kalpas, but will diligently cultivate skillful means and study various subtle and wondrous Dharma-gates.
For the sake of all sentient beings, they give rise to great compassion and remain ever free from weariness or indolence.
Their merit and wisdom are both fully perfected.
As in these various vows, they shall surely be fulfilled without fail.
If it were not so, I would not attain wondrous enlightenment.
I vow that in this very life I shall obtain the retribution of a Great Sage and acquire the six supernormal powers,
manifesting various transformations throughout the ten directions and the six realms of existence.
He universally manifests his form-body and preaches the Dharma all at once;
sentient beings who hear it attain non-retrogression and swiftly achieve Bodhi.
Were it not so, he would not take up the state of Wondrous Enlightenment.
Following this vow, the golden sutra scrolls were placed within a lapis lazuli jewel casket;
for their exposition, there were canopies and awnings made of the seven precious gems, networks of gold and silver bells, and various precious items for spreading upon the seats.
As well as all manner of implements for making offerings—
should any wicked person come wishing to steal or plunder these precious objects,
may that evil mind cause their heart to suffer from intense pain and fainting.
Furthermore, those who are deranged or speak incoherently may confess their own transgressions;
yet if they touch these objects with their hands, their hands will immediately shatter and break,
and those who look upon them with malevolent eyes will have both eyes go blind.
Those who slander with evil words shall have their mouths rendered mute and tongueless.
If those with malicious intent come wishing to cause disturbance or create obstacles,
both their legs shall break.
Or else they may suffer from leprosy,
or upon birth enter the Avīci Hell, emitting a great,
malevolent cry that resonates throughout the four directions.
To cause all evil persons to witness this event,
so that the Dharma may endure for a long time, to protect the True Dharma,
and to transform sentient beings.
I make this vow: I have no evil intent nor any envy;
may the worthy sages of the ten directions bear witness to this themselves.
Wishing to restate his intent,
he spoke these verses:
"May I attain realization of body and mind In the Prajñāpāramitā."
Possessing immeasurable meanings, you have extensively expounded them for the sake of all sentient beings;
may we attain realization within our own bodies and minds of this Prajñāpāramitā.
In the future, at the beginning of the Bhadrakalpa, may we behold Maitreya Buddha.
Among those who receive the prediction of enlightenment, may my name be foremost;
May I be fully endowed with all meditative concentrations, Supernormal powers, and the perfections;
From this may I arise and practice every ascetic austerity.
For the sake of seeking the Buddha-way, they disregard their own bodies and lives;
throughout more than five hundred million eons,
they practice asceticism for the sake of the Way, exceeding even six hundred million more.
Thus, until the Bhadrakalpa, you shall behold Maitreya Buddha and attain the knowledge of all modes;
having received the supreme prediction of certainty at the end of the Bhadrakalpa, you shall be fully endowed with the six pāramitās.
With sovereign powers of spiritual transformation, equal to those of the Buddhas of the ten directions,
I vow at the beginning of the Bhadrakalpa to preach the Dharma and deliver sentient beings;
by the power of this vow, may I turn the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma.
Abiding for immeasurable eons, eternally present and never entering nirvana,
his manifestations pervade the ten directions; he endures suffering for the sake of sentient beings in a world that is utterly pure, where all beings are born by transformation.
Furthermore, there are no three evil realms, nor are there any women;
gods and humans are of one kind, possessing the marks and signs like the World-Honored One,
fully endowed with the supernormal powers, and their wisdom is likewise the same.
Born, one is immediately able to fly; Also fully possessing all meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*) and so forth,
equal to Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, Without the sound of the two vehicles of *śrāvaka* throughout the worlds of the ten directions, And all impure, defiled lands.
Sentient beings hindered by the three obstacles do not hear the names of the Triple Gem;
through the power of great vows, he transforms them with impartial compassion.
He transforms the defiled land into a pure land, and all sentient beings become equal and level.
Devas and humans are without distinction; those who fly through the air and women who emit radiance are all transformed into men.
Having severed the three evil paths, I am known throughout the ten directions as one who travels within the great hells of the earth.
They transform and teach all those who commit offenses, causing them all to be reborn among humans and devas;
at the appropriate time, they become equal to Bodhisattvas, never becoming followers of the Two Vehicles,
nor animals, nor hungry ghosts— the transformation of their retribution is likewise the same.
If, within the worlds of the ten directions, there were even a single land where sentient beings did not abide thus, I vow not to attain perfect enlightenment. If,
within the worlds of the ten directions, there were any evil lands...
Sentient beings all hold wrong views; Stubborn and lacking a virtuous mind, I, by the power of my vows, Subdue them through spiritual transformations.
Though they are oppressed by various sufferings, I shall surely cause them to take refuge in the Triple Gem.
Or first engaging in their activities, he uses skillful means to guide them;
once their minds have been gladdened, he leads them further into the Buddha-way.
Throughout the worlds of the ten directions, there are sentient beings who are stubborn and evil.
Those in the three miserable realms and the eight difficult conditions shall all hear my name;
whether through gentle transformation or through harsh exhortation, I will surely cause them to enter the Buddha-way.
Or, first following their own inclinations, I will later cause them to sever their afflictions.
In the worlds of the ten directions, should there arise an age of weapons where nations slaughter one another, and the people suffer from famine—
may I manifest as a valiant general to subdue them and bring about peace and harmony.
The five grains shall all ripen in abundance, and the hearts of the myriad people shall be at peace.
Or again, through skillful means, he may transform them;
by employing skillful means as a deva, nāga, spirit, or ghost, he subdues evil kings and their wicked subjects.
Traversing throughout evil lands, I act according to my original vows to subdue icchantikas,
Causing them all to resolve upon the Bodhisattva mind.
Throughout the worlds of the ten directions, The Tathāgatas of the pure lands—
Amidst all these great assemblies, those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, praise my name;
I have gone to the presence of them all to make offerings and serve them, without beginning, end, or middle.
Within a single thought-moment, manifesting all physical forms and holding all offerings,
one makes offerings to all World-Honored Ones,
upholds the treasury of the Buddha-dharma, and transforms sentient beings.
Making offerings to all bodhisattvas And also making offerings to the śrāvakas,
By the power of these skillful means, May I swiftly attain Bodhi;
At the beginning of the future Bhadrakalpa, May I behold the World-Honored One Maitreya.
I vow that within this Bhadrakalpa, having perfected the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment,
I shall attain great supernormal powers; throughout the duration of this Bhadrakalpa,
from my first generation of the mind of awakening until the attainment of Bodhi.
In the interval between those two, for the sake of the Way, he practiced asceticism,
renouncing fame and profit, and abandoning all kinsmen to dwell perpetually in deep mountains, repenting of the offenses that obstruct the Path.
If you attain the power of supernatural faculties, repay the kindness of the Buddhas of the ten directions by vowing to uphold the Dharma of Śākyamuni;
may it abide eternally without extinction until the appearance of Maitreya, continuing the transformation of sentient beings without ceasing.
I vow that in this very life, I shall become a long-lived rishi endowed with the five supernormal powers;
by practicing various meditative concentrations and training in the sixth supernormal power,
I shall master all dharma-gates and attain the stage of Equal Enlightenment.
The wondrous enlightenment is eternally serene; by means of this, all Buddhas deliver sentient beings.
Among the Buddhas there is no superiority or inferiority; they merely act according to their original vows and manifest various names in accordance with the skillful means of all Buddhas.
I shall now enter the mountains to practice asceticism and repent for the grave offenses that violate the precepts and obstruct the Path—
these transgressions committed both in this life and in previous lives; I repent for them all.
For the sake of protecting the Dharma, I seek long life;
I do not wish to be born in the heavens or other realms of existence.
May all the worthy sages and holy ones assist me.
May they obtain auspicious fungi and divine elixirs;
may they cure all ailments and eliminate hunger and thirst;
and may they always practice walking meditation and cultivate the various dhyānas.
I pray to obtain a place of profound stillness in the deep mountains,
where I may fulfill this vow by means of divine elixirs;
relying on the power of external alchemy to cultivate internal alchemy.
To wish to bring peace to sentient beings while not first bringing peace to oneself—
there is no such possibility that one who is themselves bound can untie the bonds of others.
By the power of this vow to seek the Way, may I become a long-lived immortal and behold Maitreya.
Having made this vow because I do not cling to body or life, yet fearing that as an ordinary person who has not yet attained liberation,
I might lose my life and be reborn on a different path— wandering through the six realms of existence and obstructing the cultivation of the Way.
Although the nature and characteristics of all phenomena are empty and quiescent, the karmic retribution for good and evil deeds is certain.
Vowing to enter the mountains to study as an immortal, may I attain long life and strive to seek the Buddha-way;
having fulfilled this vow, may I enter the dragon palace and uphold the sutras of the Seven World-Honored Buddhas.
I shall uphold all the scriptural treasuries of all Buddhas of the past, future, and present.
In all worlds throughout the ten directions, wherever the Buddha-dharma is about to perish,
I vow to maintain and recite it so that it does not vanish, and I shall expound it extensively for the people of those lands.

In the worlds of the ten directions, when wicked bhikṣus and evil laypeople with false views see those who practice the Dharma and compete to harass and disturb them, I shall act as their aid to suppress and subdue them,
so that the preachers of the Dharma may attain peace and security, and I shall subdue these evil people to transform all sentient beings.
I bow my head to the Buddhas currently dwelling in the ten directions, To the Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Śrāvakas;
To Brahmā, Śakra, and the Four Heavenly Kings; To the Great Generals who protect the Dharma and the Vajra-holders;
To the five supernormal immortals and the Earth Deities; To the messengers of the six fast days and the officials of the underworld.
All you virtuous deities who protect the Dharma, I now repent for those sins that obstruct the Path;

may you bear witness as I pray for the removal of my delusions and faults. For the sake of seeking the Way, may I quickly attain the state of the Immortal and widely proclaim the teachings of Śākyamuni, not begrudging the passing of kalpas as I repay the Buddha’s kindness.
To protect the True Dharma, I have made this vow; Therefore, I have commissioned a *Prajñāpāramitā* Sūtra written in golden letters.
To protect all sentient beings as well as my own person, I have further commissioned a *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* Sūtra written in golden letters.
For the sake of the Mahāyāna, I have entered the deep mountains; May I swiftly achieve the state of a Great Sage.
Possessing long life and supernormal powers, you shall make offerings to all the World-Honored Ones of the ten directions;
in the future Bhadrakalpa, when Maitreya Buddha preaches the Prajñā Sūtra for the great assembly,
by the power of my vows and supernormal faculties, this precious golden scripture shall appear before you.
Emerging from the earth, they abide in mid-air; the great earth trembles as they emit light that shines universally throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
With various wondrous sounds, they address all sentient beings, extolling and praising the Dharma of Śākyamuni, so that those in the three evil paths and the eight difficulties are all liberated.
Before the assembly of Maitreya, this matter appears; before the Buddhas of the ten directions, it is likewise so.
I pray that all World-Honored Ones will proclaim my vow; by means of these causes and conditions, may I deliver sentient beings.
Having made this great vow and cultivated this practice, I pray that I may swiftly achieve the state of a Great Sage.
I seek this vow in order to protect the True Dharma; may the Buddhas take pity on me and cause it to be swiftly fulfilled.
May all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, bear witness together; may Brahmā, Śakra, and the Four Heavenly Kings bear witness;
and may the sun, moon, the lunar mansions, the stars, the Vajrapāṇis, and the ṛṣis likewise bear witness.
The five sacred peaks, the four seas, and the famous mountains, as well as all the great sage-kings, likewise bear witness.
I pray that you will protect me with compassion, causing this vow to be swiftly fulfilled;
one should constantly mind the original vow and abandon all conditioned affairs.
One should completely renounce fame, gain, and even evil disciples, both internally and externally;
one should single-mindedly seek the four bases of power (*ṛddhipāda*), the eight kinds of mastery (*vaśitā*), the five eyes (*pañcacakṣus*), and the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*).
For the sake of the Buddha’s omniscience, you should exert great diligence;
only by perfecting the power of supernormal faculties can you transform sentient beings.
You should keep in mind the Buddhas of the ten directions and the ocean-like wisdom of the great bodhisattvas.
All those monastics and laypeople in the world who earnestly invite one to lecture and provide offerings,
even to the point of forcefully urging one to preach the sutras—
they are not virtuous friends (kalyāṇamitra), but rather evil associates (pāpamitra).
Why is this? Because they are all sent by Māra;
at first, they feign diligence as if they possessed a kind heart.
Thereafter, Dousheng became enraged.
Both the good and evil Māras are unfavorable;
from this day forward, you should not trust them.
All such scholars are likewise thus;
none are to be trusted,
for they are like enemies feigning friendship.
Alas, alas! It is likewise with all the inconceivable realms of the Kṣatriya kings.
Choose, choose, choose, choose!
The Text of the Vow Established by the Great Meditation Master Si of Mount Nanyue.
